method: Legal (limited) range luma coding places reference black at code 16 and reference white at code 235 on the 8-bit scale, so 100 IRE spans 219 codes and one IRE is 2.19 codes; the 10-bit and 12-bit scales are the same signal sampled more finely, with code10 = 4 x code8 and code12 = 16 x code8, giving 64 and 940 for black and white in 10 bits and 256 and 3760 in 12 bits. Full (data) range uses the whole container instead, with code 0 at 0 IRE and code 255 at 100 IRE on the 8-bit scale, so 100 IRE spans 255 codes. The converter takes a level on one scale and a range, maps it to the 8-bit code value, and reports the level as IRE = (code8 - black) / span x 100, the equivalent 10-bit and 12-bit codes, and the percent of the full code range, code8 / 255 x 100. A level above 100 IRE is reported as that many IRE above legal white and a level below 0 IRE as that many IRE below legal black, which is the amount a legal-range encoder would clip; the nearest legal code (16 to 235 in legal range, 0 to 255 in full range) is shown for comparison. Inputs are bounded to the container: IRE -20 to 120, 8-bit 0 to 255, 10-bit 0 to 1023 and 12-bit 0 to 4095, and exponent notation is rejected rather than silently parsed. IRE is treated as a linear percentage of the encoded luma range; the tool does not model the display transfer function, chroma levels, colour gamut, HDR transfer functions, dithering, compression artefacts or noise, and it is not a waveform monitor reading. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: ITU-R BT.601 and BT.709 digital coding of the luma signal: 8-bit coding places black at 16 and white at 235 (10-bit 64 and 940, 12-bit 256 and 3760), leaving footroom and headroom outside the nominal range.
SMPTE RP 219 and EBU R 103 define the legal (broadcast-safe) range for luma as 0 to 100 IRE, with levels outside that window treated as excursions that a legaliser clips.
BT.709 full-range (data) coding, signalled by video_full_range_flag, maps code 0 to 0 IRE and code 255 to 100 IRE on the 8-bit scale, so every code carries picture information.
One IRE is 1/100 of the range between reference black and reference white, which is why 1 IRE is 2.19 8-bit codes in legal range and 2.55 codes in full range.
Code 255 in legal range sits at 109.1 IRE and code 0 at -7.3 IRE, the usual figures quoted for superwhite and the bottom of the footroom.
